title: Normalized models for strict mixed reduction
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite extensions with embedding $\iota:E\to L$, and $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $I,J$ be normalized integral direct-image models over $E,L$ [lem-sf-strict-direct-image-scalar-comparison]. There exist reduction/limit calculi $E_X,E_Y,L_X,L_Y$ with their actual coherence, scalar systems $A_X,A_Y$ and reduction models $d_X,d_Y$, normalized limit comparisons $C_E,C_L$, and normalized restriction comparison $C$, as defined in [def-weil-strict-mixed-unit-data]. Their strict projections agree with the actual Roos limit projections; their restriction, reduction, and mixed-unit finite evaluation predicates hold; and the reduction mates at every integral constructible input are isomorphisms. This statement constructs the normalization data only; it asserts no scalar/direct-image mixed-unit square.

proof.text: Work first on entire coefficient systems. Write $\mathcal R_H^W\dashv\mathcal L_H^W$ for reduction and total limit, $G_H=Rf_{*,A_{H,\bullet}}$ for system direct image, and $F_H$ for ordinary completed-ring direct image. Put $S_W=-\otimes^L_{A_{E,\bullet}}A_{L,\bullet}$ and $U_W=\operatorname{Res}_{\phi_\bullet}$, with unit $\zeta^W:1\to U_WS_W$. These functors and geometric adjunctions exist on the unbounded derived categories of the ringed sequence sites by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; extension/restriction is the adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] on that site. The canonical comparison $d:G_EU_X\xrightarrow{\sim}U_YG_L$ compares two factorizations of the same ringed-topos map. Its evaluation is precisely $\rho_{*,n}$: both are the inverse of the direct-image map from a restricted K-injective resolution to a resolution over the smaller ring, as specified in [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Moreover $d$, built from the direct-image composition isomorphisms of these two factorizations, is the conjugate of the pullback/scalar comparison $S_XV\cong VS_Y$ of the same factorizations [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction]; since system transposes evaluate to the levelwise transposes [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], $d_n$ is the level-$n$ conjugate, which by the same lemma is the K-injective comparison $\rho_{*,n}$. The coefficient unit and these comparisons are constructed on systems; no equality-detection property of evaluation is used.

proof.text:
Let $\psi_H:F_HK\xrightarrow{\sim}I_HK$ be the normalized reconstruction comparison. Its entire tower construction is $F_HK\xrightarrow{F_H(u_K)}F_H\mathcal L_H^X\mathcal R_H^XK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_H^YG_H\mathcal R_H^XK$: the second arrow is the tower direct-image/limit comparison. This is the construction and projection normalization of [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison, lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. The tower comparison compares the direct-image composites of the two factorizations of the sequence-site-to-$Y$ ringed-topos map, so it is the conjugate of the corresponding derived pullback comparison [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction]. Transpose this composite through $\mathcal R_H^Y\dashv\mathcal L_H^Y$. The result is the geometric reduction mate $\alpha_H:\mathcal R_H^YF_H\to G_H\mathcal R_H^X$, because insertion of $u_K$ and contraction with the reduction/limit counit is the square-mate formula. Consequently
$$r_H\,\mathcal R_H^Y(\psi_H)=\alpha_H.$$
Here $r_H$ is the entire system counit at $G_H\mathcal R_H^XK$, not a chosen lift of its evaluations. [lem-coef-sequence-pushforward-limit-projections, lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] identify its evaluations with the adjuncts of the actual total-limit projections, exactly the $r^H_{n,K}$ in the statement. Their invertibility on our inputs is [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible].

proof.text:
Write $C_W=-\otimes^L_{\widehat R_{E,W}}\widehat R_{L,W}$ and $\chi_W:C_W\xrightarrow{\sim}T_W$ for the canonical completion map. Let
$$s_W:\mathcal R_L^WT_W\xrightarrow{\sim}S_W\mathcal R_E^W,\qquad e_W:\mathcal R_L^WC_W\xrightarrow{\sim}S_W\mathcal R_E^W.$$
Use the comparison of [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] for $s_W$ and ordinary derived scalar association for $e_W$. Then
$$s_W\mathcal R_L^W(\chi_W)=e_W,\qquad U_W(s_W)\eta_W=\zeta^W\mathcal R_E^W.$$
To check these normalizations, use one flat-term K-flat representative $P$. Association sends $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes ab$; the composite units send $x$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes1$, by [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. The map $\chi_W$ is the quotient augmentation with zero shifted-product coordinate [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Under [lem-trf-completion-unit-strict-quotient-model] this is the actual reduction/limit unit for $C_WP$. The map defining $s_W$ is its counit followed by inverse association, so the first equation is the triangle identity in the system category [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The second follows by composing the defining ordinary mixed unit of [def-weil-mixed-reduction-unit] with this same augmentation and applying the first equation. These arguments retain both Roos coordinates and give system identities.

theorem strictMixedSystemModels
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (hl : IsUnit (l : k))
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] [IsProper f]
    (I : IntegralModel l E f) (J : IntegralModel l L f) :
  ∃ (EX : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X),
  ∃ (EY : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E Y),
  ∃ (LX : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l L X),
  ∃ (LY : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l L Y),
  ∃ (AX : CoefficientExtensionSystems l E L ι X),
  ∃ (AY : CoefficientExtensionSystems l E L ι Y),
  ∃ (dX : CoefficientExtensionReductionData l E L ι X EX LX AX),
  ∃ (dY : CoefficientExtensionReductionData l E L ι Y EY LY AY),
  ∃ (CE : LimitComparison l E f),
  ∃ (CL : LimitComparison l L f),
  ∃ (restrictionComparison : RestrictionComparison l E L ι f),
  Nonempty (CoefficientDerivedSystemCoherence l E X EX) ∧
  Nonempty (CoefficientDerivedSystemCoherence l E Y EY) ∧
  Nonempty (CoefficientDerivedSystemCoherence l L X LX) ∧
  Nonempty (CoefficientDerivedSystemCoherence l L Y LY) ∧
  (StrictProjections l E f I) ∧
  (StrictProjections l L f J) ∧
  (RestrictionEvaluation l E L ι f restrictionComparison) ∧
  (ReductionEvaluation l E f EX EY CE I) ∧
  (ReductionEvaluation l L f LX LY CL J) ∧
  (MixedEvaluation l E L ι X EX LX AX dX) ∧
  (MixedEvaluation l E L ι Y EY LY AY dY) ∧
  (∀ K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X,
    IsIso (reductionMap l E f EX EY CE I K)) ∧
  (∀ K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l L X,
    IsIso (reductionMap l L f LX LY CL J K))
